bull.b: The shift to meaningful profitability and positive free cash flow strengthens Protalix’s ability to fund operations and pipeline development internally. Strong current margins provide an operating cushion, although maintaining these results will depend on recurring product economics and less volatile revenue.

A substantial cash position combined with no debt or warrants gives Protalix flexibility to advance clinical programs, support commercialization, and absorb operating variability without immediate financing pressure. This balance-sheet structure can preserve strategic options over the next several quarters.

Growing Elfabrio sales and broader dosing and geographic approvals can expand the product’s commercial reach and reinforce its position in Fabry disease. Partner-led distribution also provides an established route to market, supporting revenue growth as access and adoption develop.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi purchasing patterns makes reported revenue less predictable and can create sharp differences between periods even when underlying demand is unchanged. This volatility complicates forecasting, cash planning, and assessment of the durability of commercial growth.

The large milestone materially boosted first-half results but does not represent recurring product sales. Comparisons could weaken once this contribution rolls off, making sustainable earnings and cash generation more dependent on ongoing Elfabrio demand and partner shipments.

A high observed antibody incidence and unresolved dosing choice could complicate PRX-115 development, affecting regimen selection, trial timing, and eventual market positioning. These uncertainties may require additional evidence before the program can progress confidently toward late-stage development.
